title: East Turkestan
capsule: The polity designated East Turkestan in this dataset corresponds to the brief Chaghatayid successor state in the Tarim Basin under Khan Yunus Khan, attested 1463–1475, asserting sovereignty over the Uyghur-inhabited oasis cities of the Eastern Tianshan region. This period falls within the fragmentation of the Chaghatai Khanate, when competing Mongol successor princes contested control of Moghulistan and the Tarim; Yunus Khan, based in the western sector, periodically extended authority eastward. The territory was never a consolidated state in the administrative sense but a contested zone whose control shifted among Chaghatayid factions. The designation 'East Turkestan' as a political concept became prominent only in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries; for this period it describes the eastern Tarim basin as a distinct administrative unit within the late Chaghatayid framework.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial attribution for this 1463–1475 interval is weakly attested; the region is documented primarily through later Timurid and Ming Chinese sources that provide only approximate boundaries for competing Chaghatayid successor claims.
